description:
Saves a new career journal entry to the user's GigHQ profile. Use this to document professional achievements, projects, skills acquired, or reflections tied to a specific role.

Entry types:
  1 = achievement — a concrete win, result, or impact (default)
  2 = project — a specific initiative the user owned or contributed to
  3 = skill_acquired — a new skill, tool, or capability gained
  4 = reflection — a lesson learned or professional observation

Tip: if the user hasn't specified a role, call `list_experiences` first, present the options, and ask which role this entry belongs to. Then pass the confirmed integer ID as `experience_id`.
experience_id is optional — entries without one are valid but less useful for resume generation and interview prep, since they can't be linked to a specific role.

STAR content (achievement entries): walk the user through their story in order, one piece at a time — don't interrogate with a checklist — and confirm you have all four parts before saving:
  Situation: the context or challenge beforehand
  Task: what specifically needed to be done or the goal to achieve
  Action: the concrete steps actually taken
  Result: the outcome, ideally with (1) scale of action: how much, how many, what scope (team size, users, codebase size, budget, requests/sec, etc.), (2) direct result: the measurable outcome (latency reduced by X%, errors down by Y, shipped Z weeks ahead of schedule), and (3) organizational impact: what that result meant for the business, team, or users (saved $X, unblocked N engineers, contributed to Y% revenue growth)
Write `description` as a well-structured STAR narrative in the user's own voice. An unlabeled but complete narrative is fine and preferred when the user wants it — do not force the labels "Situation:", "Task:", "Action:", and "Result:" into the saved text. Downstream tools use the content, not those labels.
If the Result's numbers are genuinely unavailable, note that in the description and ask the user to follow up later via update_career_entry.
Project entries benefit from the same Result-quantification numbers but don't need the full STAR structure.
Put the quantified numbers from Result in the `metrics` field as well — not buried only in the description.

context.description: A few words on why you are calling this tool, for the server developer's analytics. Describe people and things by role, such as "a customer". Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or other personal details.

conversation_id.description: The conversation_id this server returned earlier in this conversation, unchanged, including after later user messages. Omit it if you have none. Recorded for the server developer's analytics.

description.description: Full narrative in the user's own words. For achievement entries, write a well-structured STAR story covering situation, task, action, and result. An unlabeled narrative in the user's own voice is fine and preferred when the user wants it; do not require the labels Situation:/Task:/Action:/Result:. For other types, capture the what, why, and impact — not bullet points.

entry_date.description: ISO 8601 date when this happened, e.g. '2024-03-15'. Defaults to today if omitted.

experience_id.description: Optional. Links the entry to one of the user's roles. experience_id is the integer ID of one of the user's own work experience records (a role on their GigHQ profile). Get valid IDs from `list_experiences` (or the gighq://experience resource), which returns each role's experience_id, title, and company; entries already linked to a role show it as experience_id in `list_career_entries` and `get_career_entry`. Never guess or reuse an ID from another user. GigHQ rejects IDs that aren't the user's own. Omit it if the user says the entry isn't tied to a specific role.

llm_model.description: The model identifier you are running as, for example "claude-opus-4-8" or "gpt-5.2". Pass "unknown" if you are not certain. Recorded for the server developer's analytics.

metrics.description: Three-number quantification: (1) scale of action, (2) direct result, (3) organizational impact. E.g. 'Serving 50k daily users [scale] — reduced checkout latency from 2.1s to 0.4s [result] — increased conversion rate by 12%, adding ~$180k ARR [impact]'. For skill_acquired or reflection entries this can be omitted.

tags.description: Comma-separated skill or topic tags, e.g. 'TypeScript, system design, stakeholder management'. There is no application-level limit on tag count or on the length of this field (it is stored as unbounded PostgreSQL text). Prefer skill or topic tokens; job-fit ranking treats tags as searchable text alongside the title and description.

title.description: Short headline summarising the entry (e.g. 'Led migration of payments service to microservices').

type.description: Entry type: 1=achievement, 2=project, 3=skill_acquired, 4=reflection. Pass an integer or the label string. Defaults to 1.

name: add_career_entry
